name: Brain
shortFunction: Governs all voluntary and involuntary functions; coordinates vestibular adaptation to microgravity, monitors cognitive readiness and SAS symptoms.
source: NASA HRP Behavioral Health & Performance Evidence Report [Placeholder — Eman & Moazzama]
description: Cephalad fluid shift in microgravity elevates intracranial pressure, potentially causing neuro-ocular syndrome, impaired cognition, and vestibular dysfunction.
countermeasures: Circadian entrainment lighting, 8.5-hour sleep windows, cognitive performance batteries, blue-light glasses post-wakeup.

name: Eye
shortFunction: Monitors visual acuity changes driven by intracranial pressure elevation and optic disc edema (Spaceflight-Associated Neuro-ocular Syndrome).
source: NASA SANS (Spaceflight Associated Neuro-ocular Syndrome) Evidence Book [Placeholder — Eman & Moazzama]
description: SANS affects ~40% of long-duration ISS crew. Elevated ICP flattens posterior globes and causes choroidal folds and hyperopic shifts.
countermeasures: Inflight optical coherence tomography, fundoscopic imaging, intraocular pressure monitoring.

name: Neck & Cervical Spine
shortFunction: Supports cranial mass in microgravity; cervical spine decompresses without gravitational loading, potentially altering disc geometry.
source: NASA HRP Spinal Health Evidence Book [Placeholder — Eman & Moazzama]
description: Astronauts commonly report cervical discomfort and height gains of 2–3 cm due to spinal elongation from intervertebral disc expansion.
countermeasures: Ergonomic workstation alignment, targeted cervical and scapular stabilization exercises.

name: Shoulder
shortFunction: Rotator cuff and glenohumeral joint integrity essential for EVA handhold operations and free-floating translation tasks.
source: NASA JSC EVA Injury Surveillance Report [Placeholder — Eman & Moazzama]
description: EVA shoulder injuries are the most common musculoskeletal issue in spaceflight. Pressurized suit gloves and arm restraints impose abnormal torques.
countermeasures: Pre-EVA glove fit checks, rotator cuff strengthening, restricted above-shoulder reach angles during EVA.

name: Heart
shortFunction: Monitors resting heart rate, rhythm stability, and cardiac output under microgravity cephalad fluid redistribution and cardiovascular deconditioning.
source: NASA SFMO Flight Rule MED-B04 — Cardiac Telemetry Monitoring [Placeholder — Eman & Moazzama]
description: Cardiac mass decreases ~10% over 6 months in microgravity due to reduced preload. Orthostatic intolerance upon return is a primary risk.
countermeasures: LBNP sessions, 2.5h daily aerobic countermeasures (T2 treadmill, cycle ergometer), fluid and electrolyte loading pre-landing.

name: Lung
shortFunction: Tracks pulmonary ventilation efficiency and core temperature coupling in a closed spacecraft atmosphere with impaired convective cooling.
source: NASA ECLSS Physiological Standards & Thermoregulation Manual [Placeholder — Eman & Moazzama]
description: Uniform ventilation-perfusion distribution in microgravity differs from Earth; reduced convective cooling causes core temperature elevation known as 'space fever'.
countermeasures: Cabin airflow velocity adjustments, hydration maintenance, post-exercise active ventilation cycles.

name: Liver
shortFunction: Central metabolic hub for glucose homeostasis, protein synthesis, and detoxification — all altered by microgravity-induced insulin resistance.
source: NASA Evidence Book: Altered Nutrition and Insulin Sensitivity in Spaceflight [Placeholder — Eman & Moazzama]
description: Hepatic glycogen dynamics and gluconeogenesis rates are disrupted by reduced physical loading and altered circadian rhythm in microgravity.
countermeasures: Structured macronutrient timing, low-glycaemic-index foods, telemetry glucose check-in protocol.

name: Stomach
shortFunction: Gastric motility and acid secretion are altered by microgravity and stress, raising reflux and nausea risk during early mission adaptation.
source: NASA Space Motion Sickness & GI Adaptation Evidence Book [Placeholder — Eman & Moazzama]
description: Space motion sickness affects ~50% of crew in the first 72 hours. Altered gastric emptying and vagal tone changes can persist through the mission.
countermeasures: Promethazine prophylaxis during adaptation, structured meal timing, anti-nausea acupressure wristbands.

name: Kidney
shortFunction: Regulates fluid balance, electrolyte homeostasis, and erythropoietin production — all significantly altered by cephalad fluid shift.
source: NASA HRP Renal Stone Risk & Fluid Regulation Evidence [Placeholder — Eman & Moazzama]
description: Elevated urinary calcium from bone resorption increases renal stone risk. Reduced plasma volume triggers suppressed ADH and altered renin–angiotensin axis.
countermeasures: High fluid intake target (>2L/day), potassium citrate supplementation, ultrasound renal stone screening.

name: Intestines
shortFunction: Nutrient absorption and gut microbiome composition are altered by radiation, microgravity, and confined diet — affecting overall metabolic balance.
source: NASA Space Microbiome Project & GI Radiation Risk Evidence [Placeholder — Eman & Moazzama]
description: Gut microbiome diversity decreases over long missions. Altered transit time and reduced mechanical loading change absorption efficiency of key nutrients.
countermeasures: Probiotic supplements, diverse fiber intake, radiation shielding of habitability modules.

name: Spine
shortFunction: Intervertebral disc expansion and paraspinal muscle deconditioning increase risk of herniation upon return to gravity.
source: NASA HRP Spine Health & Back Pain Inflight Evidence [Placeholder — Eman & Moazzama]
description: Astronauts gain 2–5 cm in height during spaceflight from disc expansion. Post-landing disc herniation rates are elevated in the first weeks.
countermeasures: Core stabilization exercises, anti-gravity treadmill adaptation, structured post-flight rehabilitation program.

name: Pelvis
shortFunction: Load-bearing pelvic architecture undergoes bone mineral density loss without gravitational weight-bearing stimulus in microgravity.
source: NASA HRP Bone Density & Fracture Risk Evidence Book [Placeholder — Eman & Moazzama]
description: The pelvis loses 1–1.5% bone mineral density per month in microgravity. ARED resistive exercise partially mitigates this loss.
countermeasures: High-intensity ARED squats, vitamin D and calcium supplementation, bisphosphonate pharmacological countermeasures.

name: Upper Arm
shortFunction: Upper arm muscle mass and bone density maintained through ARED and EVA loading; critical for hand-over-hand translation in zero-g.
source: NASA EVA Dexterity & Upper Extremity Biomechanics Report [Placeholder — Eman & Moazzama]
description: Without gravitational loading, type II fast-twitch muscle fibers atrophy faster. EVA tasks compensate partially but create asymmetric stress.
countermeasures: ARED cable curls and extensions, resistive bungee training, pre-EVA dynamic warm-up protocol.

name: Forearm
shortFunction: Forearm endurance critical for EVA glove manipulation; pressurized glove fatigue is the most cited EVA discomfort.
source: NASA EVA Injury Surveillance & Glove Ergonomics Study [Placeholder — Eman & Moazzama]
description: Pressurized glove opposition forces cause forearm flexor fatigue and hand numbness after 4+ hours of EVA, raising tether-release error risk.
countermeasures: Hand-grip dynamometer conditioning, optimized glove fit protocol, forearm stretching post-EVA.

name: Hand
shortFunction: Fine motor dexterity for instrument operation, EVA tether clips, and repair tasks — impaired by pressurized suit glove resistance.
source: NASA Human Factors Dexterity & Fine Motor Task Research [Placeholder — Eman & Moazzama]
description: Fine motor performance degrades measurably under pressurized gloves. Microgravity itself modestly impairs proprioception in finger tasks.
countermeasures: Pre-EVA grip training, optimized glove thermal lining, ergonomic tool handle design for pressurized operation.

name: Hip
shortFunction: Hip joint bone mineral density and cartilage integrity decline without compressive axial loading from body weight.
source: NASA Osteoporosis & Joint Degeneration Evidence [Placeholder — Eman & Moazzama]
description: Hip bone density loss parallels pelvis loss at ~1% per month. The femoral neck is particularly vulnerable to stress fractures upon re-loading.
countermeasures: ARED hip abductor exercises, vibration plate exposure, bisphosphonate prophylaxis for missions >6 months.

name: Femur (Thigh)
shortFunction: Monitors quadriceps mass, femoral bone density, and venous return competence — all critically affected by absence of weight-bearing.
source: NASA HRP Bone Density Loss & Countermeasure Protocols [Placeholder — Eman & Moazzama]
description: The femur loses bone density at the proximal shaft and neck. Quadriceps cross-sectional area decreases ~10–15% over a 6-month mission.
countermeasures: ARED squats and leg press, T2 treadmill loading with harness, vibration platform sessions.

name: Knee
shortFunction: Knee cartilage and ligament integrity monitored for deconditioning-related laxity and articular cartilage thinning.
source: NASA Joint Health & Cartilage Degeneration Risk Assessment [Placeholder — Eman & Moazzama]
description: Without compressive loading, articular cartilage hydration and proteoglycan content can decrease over long missions. Post-flight landing loads shock the knee.
countermeasures: Knee-focused ARED loading protocols, harness-treadmill impact loading, pre-landing reloading gradients.

name: Lower Leg
shortFunction: Calf muscles (soleus, gastrocnemius) are the most rapidly atrophying muscle groups in microgravity; venous pump function compromised.
source: NASA Calf Atrophy & Venous Return Risk Evidence [Placeholder — Eman & Moazzama]
description: Soleus muscle CSA decreases ~15–20% over 6 months. This impairs post-flight venous return and increases orthostatic intolerance risk.
countermeasures: ARED calf raises, LBNP device sessions to stimulate lower-body venous pooling adaptation, anti-g suit familiarization.

name: Foot
shortFunction: Foot plantar sensation and arch integrity alter without weight-bearing; first post-landing steps carry injury risk.
source: NASA Post-Flight Locomotion & Foot Reloading Evidence [Placeholder — Eman & Moazzama]
description: Plantar mechanoreceptors downregulate sensitivity during spaceflight. First post-landing steps on Earth are painful and carry ankle sprain risk.
countermeasures: Vibrotactile foot stimulator insoles, proprioceptive balance board training, structured landing-day locomotion protocol.

name: Skin & Integument
shortFunction: Primary barrier against space radiation and microbial infection; skin healing and barrier function alter in microgravity confinement.
source: NASA Space Dermatology & Radiation Skin Risk Evidence [Placeholder — Eman & Moazzama]
description: Galactic cosmic radiation increases DNA damage risk in skin cells. Confined habitat reduces skin microbiome diversity and raises contact dermatitis risk.
countermeasures: High-SPF barrier UV protection during window exposure, skin microbiome probiotic support, wound care kit in medical supplies.
